messages.subject: Is it possible to get two sleep-onset and wakeup time for a pariticular day?
parts:
Hello everyone,

Hope all is well.

First of all, thank you very much Vincent van Hees for the great work on GGIR. This is Ali  I'm currently trying to get GGIR to use a sleep log & I included the following arguments in the GGIR function:

rm(list=ls())
graphics.off()
#===========================================
f0  = 1 
f1 = 1  process until the last file)
mode= c(1,2,3,4,5)

outputdir= "C:/Users/gulsa/Documents/R/GGIR/GGIR Proj"
studyname= "Data"
#===========================================

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#-----------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode=mode,
             datadir=datadir,
             outputdir=outputdir, 
             studyname=studyname,

             f1=f1, 
             overwrite = TRUE, 
             do.imp= TRUE,
             idloc=2,

             storefolderstructure=FALSE,
             #---------------------------------
             # Part 1 parameter
             #---------------------------------

             do.cal=TRUE, 
             do.enmo= TRUE, 
             do.anglez= TRUE, 
             chunksize=1, 
             printsummary=TRUE,
             #---------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters:
             #---------------------------------

             ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,
             hrs.del.end=0,
             maxdur=8, 
             includedaycrit= 16, 
             M5L5res = 10, 
             winhr= c(5,10), 
             qlevels=c(c(1380/1440), c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,8,21,24), 
             ilevels= c(),
             iglevels= TRUE,
             mvpathreshold=c(100), 
             bout.metric= 4,
             #---------------------------------
             # Part 3 parameters:
             #---------------------------------
             anglethreshold=5,
             timethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear= TRUE, 
             do.part3.pdf= TRUE,
             #---------------------------------
             # Part 4 parameters:
             #---------------------------------
             excludefirstlast= FALSE, 
             excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE, 
             includenightcrit=16, 
             def.noc.sleep =c(1), 
             #loglocation= "C:..............",
             outliers.only=FALSE,
             criterror=4,
             relyonsleeplog=FALSE,
             #relyonguider = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum= TRUE,  
             #sleeplogidnum= FALSE,
             colid=1, 
             coln1=2, 
             do.visual= TRUE,
             outliers.only = FALSE,
             #criterror = 4,
             nnights=9,
             #----------------------------------
             # Part 5 parameters:
             #----------------------------------
             excludefirstlast.part5=FALSE,
             save_ms5rawlevels=FALSE,
             threshold.lig=c(30), 
             threshold.mod=c(100), 
             threshold.vig=c(400),
             boutcriter=0.8,
             boutcriter.in=0.9, 
             boutcriter.lig=0.8, 
             boutcriter.mvpa=0.8, 
             boutdur.in=c(1,10,30), 
             boutdur.lig=c(1,10),  
             boutdur.mvpa=c(10), 
             timewindow=c("WW"), 
             #----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #----------------------------------
              do.report=c(2,4,5), 
             visualreport=TRUE,
             dofirstpage=TRUE, 
             viewingwindow=2) 

The results (attachment below) for day 6 show that the participant was asleep at two different time periods from 5 - 9 pm and 2 am- 6 am. Only the first period was taken into consideration and I couldn't figure out why that was the case. I was wondering what happens in this instance.  

Best,
Ali

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Is it possible to get two sleep-onset and wakeup time for a pariticular day?
parts:
Hi Ali,

It is not possible at the moment to extract two sleep period time windows in a day. GGIR only extracts the longest sleep period.

Let me know if you are interested in supporting the development of functionality to extract multiple sleep periods.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
